native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Original research papers in Experimental Economics have an average length of 28.00 pages, whereas original papers in Psychology have an average length of approximately 11.23 pages (within the Reproducibility Project: Psychology, RPP) or 11.16 pages (combining Cognitive and Social Psychology disciplines), demonstrating that Experimental Economics papers are significantly longer than Psychology papers.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded meta-regression study dataset, identified unique original studies by paper title and discipline, computed descriptive statistics (mean, SD, median, IQR, 95% CI) for Experimental Economics and Psychology (both RPP project and Cognitive/Social discipline definitions, at paper and row level), and conducted Welch t-tests and Mann-Whitney U tests.
